guide.title: Flows, Automations and AI Agents
guide.intro: Three building blocks, each for a different job. They work together; none replaces the others.

flows.title: Flows (Bot Studio)
flows.what: A conversation the customer clicks through: menus, buttons, lists, questions. It waits for each answer and remembers where the customer is.
flows.use: welcome menus, project selection, lead questions, then handing to sales.

automations.title: Automations
automations.what: Background rules: when something happens, do steps. They don't wait for answers; they can wait for time.
automations.use: tagging, assignment, reminders and drips, pipeline deals, webhooks, follow-ups.

ai.title: AI Agents
ai.what: Answers free-text questions from your knowledge base, hands off to a person when unsure.
ai.use: "Is parking included?", "What are the timings?" and other open questions.

guide.order1: Flows go first. If a flow handles the message, it owns it.
guide.order2: Automations run next. Message triggers are skipped when a flow handled the message; lifecycle triggers (first message, tag added…) still run.
guide.order3: AI auto-reply goes last — only for typed text nothing else handled, with no human assigned and no per-message automation active.
guide.tip1: Use the Test button in a flow to see exactly who answers a message.
guide.tip2: Put long follow-ups (days) in an Automation, not in a menu flow.
guide.tip3: "Assign agent" keeps the bot running; "Handoff" stops it and passes the chat to a person.
guide.tip4: The same keyword on a flow and an automation: the flow wins and the automation's keyword trigger is skipped.
